name: Network state
plain: Lets the app see whether the device is online and what kind of network.
meaning: Shows online status and network type; slightly useful for fingerprinting. Auto-granted.

android.note: Provides transport type, metered state and bandwidth estimates.

ios.note: Reports path status, interface type and Low Data Mode.

limits.headline: Can see if your phone is online and what kind of network it uses
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app loads or the network changes
can: Check if the phone is online
See the network type, metered state and rough speed estimate
Notice Low Data Mode on iPhone
cannot: See which Wi-Fi name you are on without location permission
See what you send or receive
limits.differs: Android needs a normal permission granted at install. iPhone needs none.

story.what_it_is: An app can see whether your phone is online and what kind of network it is on.

marketing.name: Connectivity status
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps check if you are online and on what kind of network.

marketing.name: Network framework
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps watch whether a connection is up and what type it is.

story.for_you: You do not see it. You notice an offline banner or an app that retries when the signal returns. Apps get this without asking.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to avoid errors, save data and switch between online and offline mode. It adds a small amount to a device profile, but the value is low.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows 'Connecting' and sends your queued messages the moment you are online.
A music app switches to offline mode and plays downloaded songs when you lose signal.
A mobile game pauses a match and tries to reconnect when the network drops.
A live stream app lowers quality when your network becomes weaker.
A notes app saves changes on the phone and syncs when you are back online.
A tracker logs when your connection changes, which hints at your daily path.

story.android_note: Android grants this as a normal permission at install, with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone needs no permission for this, and apps can watch changes live.

technical_bounds: No access to nearby networks without location permission

linkedin.how: Exodus lists Cedexis Radar in LinkedIn Android reports (4.1.1012 snippet). Radar is a real-user network measurement SDK used to pick CDNs; purpose in LinkedIn's app is inferred.

history.change: Network request APIs refined; NetworkCallback preferred
